subject: Tyska
title: Family and numbers
sourceSummary: Family words, possessive pronouns, and the numbers 0–100.

questions.opener: Compare with "der Bruder", which you may already know.
questions.explanation: "Die Schwester" means sister. "Der Bruder" means brother.

questions.opener: "Groß" means big/old, and the word is plural.
questions.explanation: "Der Großvater" is grandfather and "die Großmutter" is grandmother. "Die Großeltern" in the plural means grandparents together.

questions.prompt: Choose the right word: "___ Mutter heißt Rosa." (My mom's name is Rosa.)
questions.opener: "Die Mutter" is feminine, and the possessive is conjugated to match.
questions.explanation: "Meine" is the feminine form of "my" and matches "Mutter" (feminine). "Mein" is used for masculine/neuter, "dein" is "your", and "sein" is "his".

questions.prompt: How do you write the number 15 in letters?
questions.explanation: "Fünfzehn" is 15 (fünf + zehn). "Vierzehn" is 14, "sechzehn" is 16, and "zwölf" is 12.

questions.opener: In German, the ones digit is said BEFORE the tens digit: "seven-and-thirty".
questions.explanation: "Sieben" (7) + "und" (and) + "dreißig" (30) = "siebenunddreißig" = 37. Unlike Swedish or English, German says the ones digit before the tens digit.

questions.prompt: Correct the error: "Mein Bruder heißt Sofia und ist vierzehn Jahre alt." (The name refers to a girl.)
questions.opener: The word for brother versus sister changes with gender — and so does the possessive.
questions.answer: Meine Schwester heißt Sofia und ist vierzehn Jahre alt.
steps: Sofia is a girl's name, so it should be "Schwester" (sister), not "Bruder" (brother).
Since "Schwester" is feminine, the possessive must also be feminine: "meine", not "mein".
The rest is correct: "heißt Sofia und ist vierzehn Jahre alt" (is named Sofia and is fourteen years old).

questions.prompt: Which family words, possessive pronouns, and numbers should you know at grade 7 level in German?
questions.opener: The family, who it belongs to, and counting to a hundred.
questions.answer: Family: die Mutter/der Vater = mom/dad · der Bruder/die Schwester = brother/sister · der Großvater/die Großmutter = grandfather/grandmother · der Sohn/die Tochter = son/daughter · der Cousin/die Cousine = cousin. Possessives (nominative): mein/meine = my · dein/deine = your · sein/seine = his · ihr/ihre = her. Numbers: 0 null, 1 eins, 5 fünf, 10 zehn, 11 elf, 12 zwölf, 15 fünfzehn, 20 zwanzig, 21 einundzwanzig, 37 siebenunddreißig, 50 fünfzig, 100 hundert.
